name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 13 points on the partisan baseline
Jim Clyburn is a long-serving incumbent with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger John Peterson has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Clyburn near 96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Clyburn: the district leans Democratic by double digits, he holds incumbency and a roughly $1.6 million cash advantage, and his opponent has shown no measurable fundraising. Markets agree, pricing him around 96%, so the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any sign of a serious challenger fundraising push or unexpected incumbent trouble would be the main thing to watch, though neither is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District is a solidly Democratic seat, leaning about 13 points toward Democrats at the baseline. Jim Clyburn, one of the longest-serving members of the House and a top party leader, is seeking reelection with more than $1.6 million on hand. His Republican opponent, John Peterson, has reported no fundraising and little visible campaign activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets, which price Clyburn's chances near 96 percent. An upset would require an extraordinary shift well beyond anything visible in the current evidence.
